key_insight: LLM agents can translate natural-language home energy preferences into effective appliance schedules that closely match MILP optimization, especially when they can call tools natively.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical path to deploy conversational HEMS interfaces that reduce user friction while preserving cost savings, demand-response flexibility, and solar-aware scheduling.
method: Built a tool-calling ReAct agent using live Agile pricing, weather forecasts, PV estimates, household usage data, and retrieval-augmented knowledge.
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP ground truth across tariff, conflict, and solar-optimization scenarios.
Compared native function calling with text-parsed action interfaces to test scheduling reliability.
evidence_signal: Across tariff days, constraint conflicts, and a week-long deployment, the models achieved 100% scheduling success with native function calling and captured 96.7-98.0% of oracle savings.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply when actions must be text-parsed, so robust tool interfaces and constraint handling are critical for real deployments.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
